name: inform6
why: Inform 6 is a classic interactive fiction language with a deep, quirky history, and writing a text adventure is a real door into an unusual craft.

brief.what_it_is: Inform 6 is a compiler for Inform, a C-like design language for writing interactive fiction (text adventures), created by Graham Nelson and first released in 1993. You feed it Inform 6 source files together with the Inform 6 library, and it produces a Z-machine story file that a Z-machine interpreter can run. The README says Inform 6 is now considered stable, with only bug fixes and minor non-breaking features added, and it is also the code generator used by Inform 7. The Homebrew package also ships punyinform, pblorb, and scanblorb helpers, but the README I read does not describe them.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a continuation of a community tradition: after Infocom's Z-machine format was reverse-engineered in the late 1980s, Nelson's Inform made it practical for hundreds of free games to be written by the rec.arts.int-fiction community. It still exists as the language in its own right and as the engine underneath Inform 7.
brief.how_it_works: Source is compiled by a C program into a Z-machine story file, with the Inform 6 library supplying the standard adventure-game behaviour. The README says you need both a compiler executable and a version of the library to write a work of fiction. Pre-built executables are available, or you can build from C source with a plain C compiler.

commands_seen.context: Build the Inform 6 compiler from source on a generic Unix-like system with any C compiler.
Same build, but defining PC_WIN32 to select suitable defaults when compiling for Windows.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, you need an Inform 6 library, which is separate from the compiler. Stable library releases are on the IF Archive, and ongoing library development is in a separate GitLab project. The README says the compiler source is a plain C build with no other stated dependencies. Platform defaults are selected by defining a symbol near the top of header.h, and the README lists no first-run configuration.
brief.standout: It is a living fossil of interactive-fiction history: a small C compiler for a 1993 language that still feeds Inform 7 underneath. Its tooling is very low-level, with source compiled to Z-machine story files and no IDE, so you are writing code in a plain text editor against a library.
brief.status: Mixed. The inform6.html homepage says it is a historical reference, was last updated 24 July 2020, and has been only minimally maintained since. The GitHub compiler README says Inform 6.44 is copyright 1993-2025, development continues, and the language is stable with fixes still landing. I did not see a last-commit date or release date, so the exact status is unverified.
brief.caveats: The main website is historical and out of date, so use the README and the IF Archive for current information. Building from source needs a C compiler, and the Windows build needs a -DPC_WIN32 define. Writing an actual game also needs the separate Inform 6 library, which is not part of the compiler. The README does not describe the punyinform, pblorb, or scanblorb executables that the Homebrew package installs. The homepage was reachable and nothing I read was missing.
quotes: Inform 6 is now considered stable and only has bugs fixed and minor, non-breaking features added, but development continues.
In 1993, Graham Nelson released the first version of Inform, which compiled a somewhat C-like language ("Inform") to the Z-Machine.
In the years that followed this led to the creation of hundreds of free games by a community that had sprung up based around the Usenet group rec.arts.int-fiction.

judge.reason: Inform 6 opens a door into interactive fiction and the Z-machine: a distinctive, still-used language that turns source code into portable text adventures.

entry.title: Inform 6
entry.tldr: A 1993 compiler for writing text adventures in a C-like language, producing Z-machine story files and still serving as the engine under Inform 7.
entry.deeper_look:
Inform 6 is a compiler written in C. You give it source files in the Inform language, which looks somewhat like C, plus the Inform 6 library. It produces a Z-machine story file, the same kind of file Infocom used for its text adventures. A Z-machine interpreter then runs that file.

Graham Nelson released the first version in 1993. The README ties it to a community tradition: after the Z-machine format was reverse-engineered in the late 1980s, Inform made it practical to write new games for it. The README says this led to "hundreds of free games" from the rec.arts.int-fiction Usenet community.

The compiler does not contain the adventure-game behaviour. The library supplies parsing, rooms, objects and the standard way a text adventure responds to you, and you write your game against it. The library is a separate download, so the compiler alone is not enough to write a game. There is no IDE. You work in a plain text editor and run the compiler.

The README calls the language stable, with only bug fixes and minor non-breaking features added, though development continues. It is also the code generator underneath Inform 7, so it is still in use. The Homebrew package also installs punyinform, pblorb and scanblorb helpers, which the README does not describe.
entry.install:
brew install inform6
# The compiler does not include the Inform 6 library. Stable library releases are on the IF Archive, and development is on GitLab.
# You will also need a Z-machine interpreter to run the story files you compile.

entry.whats_unique: It is a small C compiler for a 1993 language that still feeds Inform 7 underneath. Writing against it means working directly with a language and a library, with no IDE.
entry.caveats: The homepage calls itself a historical reference last updated in July 2020, while the GitHub README says development continues, and you must fetch the separate Inform 6 library to write a real game.
